We create thriving places and connected communities. We plan, build and maintain Victoria’s transport, planning and land services. We are committed to a safe, inclusive and high-performing workplace.

The Senior Environmental Specialist leads complex environmental and land management initiatives to support safe and sustainable road network operations. Key responsibilities include advising project and maintenance teams on environmental compliance, managing biodiversity, vegetation, fire risks, pests and contaminated land, preparing strategic briefs, and delivering environmental programs. The role also leads municipal maintenance agreements, fire risk mitigation planning, contract management, stakeholder negotiations and performance reporting.

Fosters a collaborative culture, breaks down barriers to information sharing and works across teams to achieve shared outcomes.
Applies critical thinking and sound judgement to complex issues, considering broader business impacts and developing practical, sustainable solutions.
Demonstrates strong knowledge of environmental legislation, planning policies and standards, providing expert advice and ensuring compliance across projects and operations.

Description

OPEN RECRUITMENT

State Highway Administration

Lead Historian (Environmental Analyst IV)

Grade 18 (8436) SP# 26-50-11

YOU MUST APPLY ONLINE TO BE CONSIDERED FOR THIS POSITION

http://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/mdotmd

The State Highway Administration’s (SHA) Office of Planning and Preliminary Engineering (OPPE) Historic Preservation Division
is recruiting for a Lead Historian (Environmental Analyst IV)
position in Baltimore City.
This position is open to anyone who meets the minimum
and
selective
qualifications listed below. This is a position specific recruitment.
The resulting list of eligible candidates will be used to fill this vacancy or function only. You will need to reapply for any future recruitment conducted for this job classification.

Nature of work:
This position reports to the Assistant Division Chief of the Historic Preservation Division (HPD) within the Office of Planning and Preliminary Engineering (OPPE). The Lead Historian oversees the State Highway Administration (SHA) component of the Historic Highway Markers Program (a collaboration with the Maryland Historical Trust) and supports capital program compliance through historical research for project reviews under Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act.

The Lead Historian ensures HPD carries out the longstanding (since 1930) partnership between the SHA and the Maryland Historical Trust to commemorate historically significant events, people, and places along the State Highway System with commemorative markers that are thoroughly researched, coordinated with stakeholders, and works with appropriate SHA staff to ensure markers are installed in accordance with SHA safety considerations and requirements. The position also tracks needed maintenance and repair of the 800+ markers on the system and ensures ongoing review for accuracy and appropriateness by coordinating with stakeholder communities.

Additionally, the Lead Historian supports historic roadway assets such as mile markers on Maryland’s historic road system, and capital program delivery by providing research support for core functions of the historic preservation division, such as researching historic contextual information for properties being reviewed for project impacts, researching chains of title to assess historic significance and identify descendant communities as stakeholders. The position provides other similar historical expertise supporting review under the National Historic Preservation Act for project study areas and individual properties both on the roadway system and potentially affected by project elements.

MDOT offers a generous and competitive benefits package. You can learn about our amazing benefits here : MDOT Benefits Guide
.

“The State Highway Administration (SHA) has been named a Training magazine Training Awards winner for the seventh consecutive year."

Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

Education:
Possession of a Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in natural sciences, earth science, physical science, environmental science, chemistry, physics, biology, agronomy, forestry, horticultural or related sciences, geography, environmental planning, civil engineering, sociology, economics, planning, anthropology, architectural history or related fields such as ecology, landscape architecture, or environmental engineering.

Experience:
Six (6) years of experience in environmental analysis to include the development of plans, specifications, estimates, and design,

OR

six (6) years of experience in environmental management to include the development, implementation and monitoring of environmental compliance plans for air quality, storm water management, wastewater treatment, hazardous waste management, pollution prevention, solid waste management or multi-media operations.

Selective Qualification:
Candidate must meet the Secretary of the Interior’s Professional Qualifications Standards published in 48 Fed. Reg. 44738-39 (including any succeeding revisions to the regulations) in the fields of archaeology, architectural history, and/or history to carry out its historic preservation programs and responsibilities, as noted below:

History

The Minimum Professional Qualifications In History Are a Graduate Degree In History Or Closely Related Field; Or a Bachelor's Degree In History Or Closely Related Field Plus One Of The Following:

At least two years of full-time experience in research, writing, teaching, interpretation, or other demonstrable professional activity with an academic institution, historic organization or agency, museum, or other professional institution; or
Substantial contribution through research and publication to the body of scholarly knowledge in the field of history.

Archeology

The minimum professional qualifications in archeology are a graduate degree in archeology, anthropology, or closely related field plus:

At least one year of full-time professional experience or equivalent specialized training in archeological research, administration, or management;
At least four months of supervised field and analytic experience in general North American archeology, and
Demonstrated ability to carry research to completion.

In addition to these minimum qualifications, a professional in prehistoric archeology shall have at least one year of full-time professional experience at a supervisory level in the study of archeological resources of the prehistoric period. A professional in historic archeology shall have at least one year of full-time professional experience at a supervisory level in the study of archeological resources of the historic period.

Architectural History

The Minimum Professional Qualifications In Architectural History Are a Graduate Degree In Architectural History, Art History, Historic Preservation, Or Closely Related Field With Coursework In American Architectural History Or a Bachelor's Degree In Architectural History, Art History, Historic Preservation Or Closely Related Field Plus One Of The Following:

At least two years of full-time experience in research, writing, or teaching in American architectural history or restoration architecture with an academic institution, historical organization or agency, museum, or other professional institution; or
Substantial contribution through research and publication to the body of scholarly knowledge in the field of American architectural history.

Preferred Qualifications:

The ideal candidate will possess the following:

At least two years experience in professional historical research
Professional experience in fields related to History, Public History, Anthropology, Archaeology, Historic Preservation, Architectural History, Transportation Planning or similar.
Working knowledge of federal and state environmental statutes, laws, regulations, policy procedures, etc., especially those related to Section 106 compliance, transportation planning and cultural resources.
Knowledge of the principles, practices and methods for conducting historical research with a public focus and/or transportation compliance focus.
Knowledge of techniques of standard research methodology including data collection, organization, analysis and result presentation.
Working knowledge of government organization and operations, with particular emphasis on transportation agencies
Strong writing and editing skills, both technical and for general audience
Skilled in customer service to represent the agency, provide information and resolve conflicts

Notes:

Possession of a master's degree in one of the disciplines required may be substituted for one year of the required non-supervisory experience.
Possession of a doctorate's degree in one of the disciplines required may be substituted for two years of the required non-supervisory experience.
U.S. Armed Forces military service experience as defined under the Minimum Qualifications may be substituted for the required experience on a year-for-year basis.

Licenses & Certifications

None.

Additional Information

Special Requirements:

Per legal agreement with FHWA and Maryland Historical Trust, candidate must meet Secretary of Interior requirements for Architectural History, Archaeology or History (graduate degree or equivalent experience in relevant related field).

Ability to conduct historical research to a high professional standard, including source evaluation, work with archives and other specialized sources, synthesis, and effective writing and critical thinking skills
Ability to apply state and federal regulatory policy, procedures and guidelines, especially those pertaining to cultural resources and historic preservation in transportation.
Ability to manage databases and GIS information related to roadway marker program.
Ability to effectively communicate with external stakeholders on roadway marker applications, content development and other coordination.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relations with others including internal and external teams.
Ability to interpret maps, plans and specifications.
Ability to coordinate work with contractors and technical personnel.
Ability to conduct field analysis.

Resumes will not be accepted in lieu of a completed application. To receive credit for your work history and credentials you must list the information in the online DTS-1 application form. added.description:
We Are The People Who Give Possibilities Purpose

BD is one of the largest global medical technology companies in the world. Advancing the world of health™ is our Purpose, and it’s no small feat. It takes the imagination and passion of all of us—from design and engineering to the manufacturing and marketing of our billions of MedTech products per year—to look at the impossible and find transformative solutions that turn dreams into possibilities.

Job Description

Job Responsibilities:

Lead and provide strategic directions to team members supporting medical device development, regulatory submissions, and product lifecycle management activities.
Mentor and develop scientific staff while fostering technical excellence, innovation, and a culture of compliance and continuous improvement.
Represent Toxicology and Biocompatibility in management and leadership forums, providing expert guidance on strategy, risk assessment, regulatory requirements, and global submission impacts.
Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) on new product development, innovation, and sustaining projects, supporting product teams with biocompatibility, toxicology, chemistry, and regulatory expertise.
Review and approve change control documentation and product modifications to ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, quality, and safety requirements.
Act as Sponsor Representative for biocompatibility and chemistry studies, providing scientific oversight for the design, execution, interpretation, and reporting of preclinical and biological safety evaluations.
Author, review, and approve Biological Evaluation Plans (BEPs), Biological Evaluation Reports (BERs), toxicological risk assessments, and related documentation supporting FDA, EU MDR, and other global regulatory submissions.
Representing the organization on industry standards committees and professional working groups, including AAMI and ISO 10993 committees, influencing standards development and applying emerging requirements within the organization.
Lead regulatory and standards gap assessments, evaluating the impact of evolving medical device regulations and standards on products, processes, and compliance strategies.
Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to harmonize and continuously improve risk assessment methodologies, biological safety processes, and supporting documentation across the product portfolio.
Support global regulatory, quality, and compliance initiatives by providing scientific and strategic toxicology and biocompatibility expertise.

Required Skills/Experience

Required Bachelor’s degree in Toxicology or closely related scientific field with minimum of 10 years of relevant experience; will also consider - Master’s Degree with minimum of 8 years relevant experience; OR Ph.D. with minimum of 6 years relevant experience.
Board certification in toxicology required, such as Diplomate of the American Board of Toxicology (DABT) or European Registered Toxicologist (ERT) is required
Broad expertise in biology, biocompatibility, toxicology, and chemistry including current methodologies, evaluation techniques and the ISO 10993 series of standards.
Experience working in an FDA-regulated medical device environment is required.
Demonstrated ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with a diverse network of internal and external stakeholders across national and international settings.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, and other business software tools.
Excellent scientific writing and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical and regulatory concepts for diverse audiences.
Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to effectively manage competing priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams and build productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Strong interpersonal, leadership, and influencing skills supported by a customer-focused mindset and commitment to delivering high-quality outcomes.
Sound scientific judgment and analytical skills, with the ability to evaluate complex issues and provide practical, risk-based recommendations to support business objectives.

Preferred Skills/Experience

Experience in a Good Laboratory Practice (GLP) preclinical environment preferred.
